/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 37-year-old man with a history of depression has a two-year history of slowly worsening movement abnormalities characterized by rapid, involuntary, nonrepetitive movements involving his face, trunk, and limbs presents to clinic. He has also noted worsening of his depression, along with symptoms of increased anxiety and irritability. During the interview, his wife explains that he has suffered cognitive decline, most notably in the realm of executive function. On family history, you discover that his father suffered from a similar illness before dying at the age of 44. What would be the expected findings on brain MRI?

Options:
A. Normal brain MRI
B. Atrophy of the caudate nucleus
C. Periventricular high-signal intensity lesions on FLAIR sequence
D. Atrophy of the hippocampi
E. A ring-enhancing lesions after administration of radiocontrast

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question concerns Huntington's disease, a neurocognitive disorder with movement and psychiatric symptoms, which falls within the scope of neurocognitive disorders."}
